newsitem.title: UK: UK govt redeems election pledge on environment.
newsitem.headline: UK govt redeems election pledge on environment.

text.p: The new Labour government, showing it is serious about green issues, is setting up a House of Commons select committee to help ensure ministries meet high environmental protection standards, officials said on Tuesday.

Establishment of the parliamentary environmental audit committee redeems a pledge in Labour's election manifesto, which said that protection of the environment cannot be the sole responsibility of any one department of state.

Officials announced the move as Prime Minister Tony Blair and other senior ministers met environmental and third-world aid lobby groups to discuss Britain's stance at this month's United Nations conference in New York to follow up the Rio Earth Summit.
The cabinet's environmental committee will meet for the first time on Wednesday under the chairmanship of Deputy Prime Minister John Prescott, who is also Environment Secretary.
